summary: Opening Day is the day professional baseball leagues begin their regular season, typically in the first week of April for MLB and most minor leagues. The note traces how MLB moved away from traditional Monday openers in 2011 and 2012 to avoid the World Series running into November, returned to Mondays through 2017, and then scheduled all 30 teams to open on March 29, 2018.
one_line: Opening Day marks the start of the professional baseball regular season, with MLB's opening dates shifting between 2011 and 2018.
key_facts: Opening Day is the day on which professional baseball leagues begin their regular season.
For Major League Baseball and most minor leagues, Opening Day typically falls during the first week of April.
Most MLB teams opened the 2011 season on Thursday (March 31) or Friday (April 1) rather than the traditional Monday.
The 2011 schedule change was made to prevent the World Series from extending into November.
Most MLB teams opened the 2012 season on Thursday (April 5) or Friday (April 6).
Seasons after 2012 through 2017 returned to Monday openers for most teams.
For the 2018 season, all 30 MLB teams were scheduled to open on Thursday, March 29.
March 29, 2018 was the earliest domestic start for a regular season in MLB history.
2018 was the first time since 1968 that all major league teams were scheduled to start the season on the same day.
Two games scheduled for March 29, 2018 were rained out and postponed to Friday, March 30.
